'''Robert''' "'''Rob'''" '''Nelson''' (born August 13, 1979, in [[Denver, Colorado]])<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.explorebiodiversity.com/main/crew/RobNelson.html|accessdate=January 26, 2016|title=Rob Nelson|website=Explorebiodiversity.com|archive-date=March 30, 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160330024803/http://www.explorebiodiversity.com/main/crew/RobNelson.html|url-status=dead}}</ref> is an American biologist, documentary filmmaker, television personality and [[YouTube]]r.<ref name=Untamed>{{cite web|url=http://www.untamedscience.com/robnelson/|title=Robert Nelson - Biologist and Educator|website=Untamedscience.com|accessdate=January 26, 2016}}</ref>

He is a regular contributor to the [[Science Channel]] documentary series ''[[What on Earth? (American TV program)|What on Earth?]]'' Starting in 2017, he was the host and participating researcher of the Science Channel documentary series ''Secrets of the Underground'', whose goal was to examine long-held legendary mysteries that lie beneath the surfaces of streets, buildings, earth, salt and fresh water, etc.<ref>[https://www.imdb.com/title/tt4543056/ IMDB listing]</ref><ref>{{IMDb name|7405351}}</ref> Nelson also cohosted the popular hit [[Animal Planet]] show, ''Life After Chernobyl'' in 2015.

He holds a [[B.S.]] in biology and marine science from the [[University of Miami]], a [[M.S.]] degree in behavioral ecology from the [[University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa]], and a [[Master of Fine Arts|M.F.A.]] from the [[Montana State University]].<ref name=Untamed/> His work focused on finding ways to create the most effective science films.<ref>{{Cite thesis |title=What makes a science video engaging in today's American classroom? |url=https://scholarworks.montana.edu/xmlui/handle/1/1946 |publisher=Montana State University - Bozeman, College of Arts & Architecture |date=2011 |language=en |first=Robert P. (Robert Paul) |last=Nelson}}</ref>

He received an [[Emmy Award]] in 2014 for his work on ''Mysteries of the Driftless,'' a documentary film about the [[Driftless Area]]. He later filmed a second feature of the Mysteries of the Driftless in 2018 called ''Decoding the Driftless'', which won another Emmy Award, and won "Best Picture" at the [[Los Angeles Film Festival]] in 2019.<ref name=Untamed/>

Nelson's current work includes being the director of ''Untamed Science,'' a science documentary production company. He also hosts three [[YouTube]] channels, the most famous of which is the ''StoneAgeMan'' channel.<ref>{{cite web |title=StoneAgeMan |url=https://m.youtube.com/user/UntamedScience |website=[[YouTube]]}}</ref> His show works to help humans understand their relationship with the natural world. Rob works closely with the [[North Carolina Zoo]] to help tell animal stories.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.nczoo.org/education/educator-portal/educator-resources |title=North Carolina Zoo - Education - Educator Resources - Untamed Science|date=19 July 2018 |publisher=[[North Carolina Zoo]]}}</ref>
